descriptionChirho: Spatial correspondence indicating that one thing is positioned parallel to or directly matching another, often used in architectural descriptions of the temple or city walls (e.g., 'corresponding to the wall').
Spatial proximity indicating nearness or adjacency, describing something positioned close to or alongside another object or person, including suffixed forms ('beside them', 'opposite him').
Adversarial or confrontational positioning, indicating something set against or facing in opposition rather than mere spatial adjacency.
Used with the preposition min to indicate source or origin from a position alongside or beside something, describing movement away from an adjacent location.
Comparative sense indicating similarity or equivalence in manner, used to express that something is done in the same way as something else.
